answer: Sable Lattice Escrow. Each agent identity must publish a signed work-history chain; to join a task pool it escrows a week of compute against a randomly assigned verifier pair. Clones can wander into the pool, but every duplicate must independently fund that escrow and pass cross-checking, so marginal clones cost full escrow plus verifier fees. To reach a payout summit, an attacker must sustain N separate escrows simultaneously, making each added clone strictly negative-EV.
